topup.hyperswitchNote: Mounts the switch's Unified Checkout in place; the deposit confirms through the Hyperswitch webhook once the payment succeeds. A deployment without the rail configured hides it.

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.estimateNote: The upper bound the gateway would freeze for a request of this shape. Nothing is held or charged — a real settle never exceeds the answer.
pricing.checkpointNote: A channel-model price row, signed under the same key that signs tree heads. A bill names the version it priced under — pass that to re-sign an older price.

reports.title: Reports
reports.readError: The reports could not be read.
reports.linksError: The links could not be read.
reports.hashNote: The database keeps only its hash. Copy it now — if it is lost, revoke it and mint another.
reports.whatIsReport: A report is one downstream customer's signed bill over an ended span. Share it as a link the customer opens without an account; every row is provable against the ledger.
reports.minting: This mints a signed report for {{customer}} over {{from}} → {{to}}.
reports.spanEnded: The span must be fully ended: a report over a day still open would commit a subset that can grow.
reports.oneLink: One link that lists every report issued to a customer — for the customer who wants their history, not one bill.

log.title: Transaction log
log.readError: The log could not be read.
log.noPinnedKey: no pinned key; the deployment publishes no key for this witness
log.keyNote: The public half of the key that signs tree heads and price checkpoints. Fetching it here is convenience — a verifier pins it through a channel the operator does not control.

chat.title: Chat
chat.probeNote: messages / embeddings / rerank are billed probes, not chat
chat.hint1: Ask anything; every turn is a billed request.
chat.hint2: The wallet freezes an upper bound before the stream starts…
chat.hint3: …and settles against actual usage when it ends.

settings.title: Settings
settings.verificationSent: Verification email sent; check your inbox.
settings.displayNote: The ledger always keeps credits — this is only how the dashboard and the statement PDF render them. Set a code and a rate per credit; leave the code empty to render credits alone. The conversion is presentational — a bill's proof covers the credits, never the fiat figure.
settings.rendersAs: This organization renders credits as ≈ {{rate}} {{code}} per credit, {{decimals}} decimals.
settings.ownerOnly: (only an owner or an admin may change it)
settings.twoFactorNote: A confirmed authenticator gates every password login behind a live six-digit code — or a single-use backup code — so a stolen password alone cannot open the session.
settings.twoFactorOn: Two-factor authentication is on. Save these backup codes — they are shown this once, each works a single time.
settings.addSecretNote: Add this secret to your authenticator — scan the link or type the base32 — then prove it with a live code.
settings.liveCodeHint: the six digits the authenticator now shows
settings.turnOffHint: a live code disables the confirmed factor
settings.deleteNote: This cannot be undone. Your password confirms the deletion.
settings.deleteExplain: Deleting the account is irreversible: the email is tombstoned, sessions and API keys are revoked, memberships end — except that an organization's last owner is refused. Bills keep verifying; the ledger never carries identity. OAuth-created accounts need a real password (set one through the reset flow) to confirm this.

auth.twoFactorNote: Enter the six-digit code from your authenticator, or a single-use backup code.
auth.passwordChanged: The password was changed. All sessions were revoked.
auth.noToken: No token in the link? Request a fresh verification mail.
